 Judgment
This writ petition is filed challenging Exhibit P6 notice dated 28.7.2017 issued by the 2 nd respondent as also Exhibit P3 test report of the 4th respondent dated 25.11.2016.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Government Pleader.
3.
It is submitted that the 2nd petitioner is the Proprietor of an Oil Mill manufacturing coconut oil.
Samples of the coconut oil were collected from the 3rd petitioner's place of business by the 1 st respondent on 3.11.2016.
A fine of Rs.15,000/- was imposed on the 3 rd petitioner and a fine of Rs.50,000/- was imposed on the 1 st petitioner.
On the ground that the packet did not contain the vegetarian logo, Exhibit P3 report found that the product was misbranded.
On 28.4.2018, Exhibit P4 notice requiring the petitioners to attend a hearing before the 2 nd respondent on 19.5.2018 was issued.
Though the petitioners attended the said hearing, Exhibit P6 proceedings have been issued.

Alleging offence under Section 3(1)(zf)C(ii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short,
'the Act') read with Regulation 2.2.2:4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labeling)
Regulations, 2011.

sentences.text: It is stated that Exhibit P6, which is seen dated 28.7.2017, was received by the petitioners only on 22.9.2018.
It is therefore contended that the proceedings were issued without considering any of the contentions of the petitioners.
4. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioners that the test report which contains a finding that the article is misbranded is completely untenable in law.
It is further contended that Exhibit P6 order has been passed without giving the petitioners an opportunity of hearing, since it is dated 28.7.2017.
It is stated that there is no power in the Analyst to issue a report in the nature of Exhibit P3 and the reliance placed in Exhibits P6 on Exhibit P3 is completely misconceived.

sentences.text: The learned Government Pleader would, on the other hand, contend that the offence of misbranding is clearly made out in the instant case, since the item in question did not contain the vegetarian logo which is imperative in the case of a food article which is vegetarian by its nature.

It is stated that the 4 th respondent has all power in terms of Section 46 to consider the question whether the article is misbranded and in case such an offence is made out, the respondents are perfectly justified in issuing an order in the nature of Exhibit P6.
It is contended that notice had been issued to the petitioners by Exhibit P4 and the order had been issued after hearing the respondents as well.
It is stated that the date shown in Exhibit P6 is only a mistake and that it was rendered on 28.7.2018 and served on the petitioner soon thereafter.
6. I have considered the contentions advanced.
The question of power of the Food Analyst to enter a finding on misbranding in the test report is covered by a decision of this Court in W.P(C).35151 of 2018 and connected cases.

This Court has held that in view of the specific provisions contained in Sections 3 and 46 of the Act and the Regulations framed thereunder, the Food Analyst has the power to analyse whether a particular article of food is misbranded or not.

In the instant case, after the laboratory report has been obtained, the petitioners had been put on notice and the petitioners'
contentions considered before entering a finding of misbranding.
In case the petitioners have enough factual contentions, those could have been raised by the petitioners in a properly constituted appeal.

In view of the fact that the petitioners have preferred this writ petition on 7.11.2018, within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of the order by the petitioners, I am of the opinion that in case the petitioners have any factual contentions to raise as against Exhibit P6 order, they have to do so in a properly constituted appeal.
The time spent before this Court prosecuting the writ petition shall be exempted and any appeal preferred by the petitioners shall be considered by the respondents in accordance with law.
The writ petition is ordered accordingly.
